Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female presents with a 1-week history of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, lower abdominal pain, and recent pink urine; probable diagnosis of uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI).

History:
- Presenting complaint: Pain on urination (burning/stinging), increased urinary frequency (~1 week duration), lower abdominal ache, pink-colored urine noted today.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began just under a week ago; lower abdominal pain mainly when urinating; pink urine today.
- Progression: Ongoing, not improving, affecting ability to attend university.
- Exacerbating factors: Lower abdominal pain worsens when using the toilet.
- Relieving factors: Not mentioned.
- Associated symptoms: No nausea, vomiting, fever, or new bowel symptoms.
- Systems review: No new bowel symptoms (baseline Irritable Bowel Syndrome [IBS]; variable bowel habit but unchanged), no abnormal vaginal discharge, no back or flank pain.
- Gynecological/sexual history: Sexually active with a long-term boyfriend, on combined oral contraceptive pill (OCP); last unprotected intercourse ~1–2 weeks ago; last period 2 weeks ago.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS): Variable bowel habits; no new gastrointestinal symptoms.
- No other medical conditions reported.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Mebeverine (for IBS; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Clindamycin (details of reaction not specified).

Social History:
- University student (studying English), recently started university, lives in university halls with a flatmate; family lives nearby.
- Smoking: Denies tobacco use; tried cannabis (weed) once at a party ~1.5 weeks ago.
- Alcohol: Occasional/social drinking.
- No evidence of financial or other social stressors.

Family History:
- No history of bladder or kidney problems; no other family history of note.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/not documented (consult was remote; no examination findings stated).

Investigations:
- Urine sample to be provided for lab analysis (to check for infection and confirm diagnosis).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI)/cystitis
  - Plan: Empiric antibiotic treatment discussed (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin—medication choice not confirmed in transcript), with a three-day course suggested; urine sample to be provided for confirmatory testing and antibiotic sensitivity.
  - Advice: Maintain adequate hydration, use paracetamol for pain if needed, monitor for worsening symptoms such as fever, back pain, or vomiting (seek urgent review if these occur).
  - Follow-up: Review if symptoms persist after antibiotics or worsen; follow-up on urine culture results.
- Issue 2: IBS (background)
  - No new symptoms; continue current management with Mebeverine.
- Issue 3: Risk related to recent cannabis use
  - Advice: Avoid recreational drug use in future.

General Plan items:
- Ensure patient understands red flag symptoms for UTI complications.
- Provide instructions for urine sample submission.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs or physical examination performed/documented.
  - No specific antibiotic selected/prescribed in transcript—choice remains unclear.
  - No details of clindamycin allergy reaction.
  - No full medication reconciliation (doses/routes/frequencies not provided).
  - No menstrual or gynecological exam performed.
●	Internal conflicts:
  - Minor uncertainty around the duration of symptoms initially (3 days vs. just under a week); clarified as "just under a week."
●	Transcript quality:
  - Clear recording with some minor conversational redundancy; clinical information readily extractable. No major audio/noise concerns.
